gitCommit.subject: fix(canvas): keep image resize handles visible when child overflows frame (#1529)
gitCommit.body:
fix(canvas): keep image resize handles visible when child overflows frame (#1529)

* fix(canvas): keep frame child stationary during resize snap

handleImageTransformMove wrote the absolute `snappedPosition` directly into
`node.position()`. For images inside a Frame, the node's x/y are frame-local,
so each snap tick shoved the child by `frame.position` and accumulated the
offset during the drag — the visible "drifting" on resize.

Extract `applyTransformMoveSnap` to add snap as a local delta on the node,
and return the absolute snapped position separately for useImageDragStore.
Add regression tests covering frame-child, top-level, zero-snap, single-axis,
and accumulated-ticks cases.

* fix(canvas): enable TextV2 inline edit for frame children

FrameNode rendered TextV2 children without onDblClick and without the
isEditing flag, so double-clicking a TextV2 inside a Frame never reached
setEditingTextV2Id and the resize transformer kept covering the edit
outline. Forward both onTextV2DblClick and editingTextV2Id from
gazai-canvas, and derive isThisEditing locally to hide the transformer,
disable drag, and show the inline-edit outline — symmetric with the
top-level TextV2 render path.

* fix(canvas): keep frame-child image resize handles visible when overflowing

Image children inside a Frame had their Transformer rendered inside the
frame's clip group alongside the image, so when the image exceeded the
frame bounds the corner anchors fell outside the clip region and became
invisible/unclickable. Add a renderTransformer prop to ImageNode (default
true) that lets FrameNode suppress the internal Transformer for its
children, and render a single external Transformer at the FrameNode root
— sibling to the clip group, attached by id to the currently selected
image child — so handles stay on-screen and grabbable regardless of the
image's size. onTransform is wired directly on the external Transformer;
onTransformEnd continues to bubble through the child Group as before.

* refactor(canvas): extract deriveSelectedImageChildId with unit tests

The inline IIFE that decides which frame image child hosts the external
Transformer had seven independent guards and no test coverage, making it
easy to silently regress if a new CanvasObject variant or selection mode
is added. Extract it as a pure function with 11 unit tests pinning each
guard and the short-circuit contract. Also expand the attach-effect and
selection comments to document the id-based lookup convention and the
"why" behind each exclusion.

* docs(canvas): document external child-image Transformer in frame.md

Add the new render node to the Rendering Architecture section, explain
why it lives outside the clip group (mirrors the border's reason), and
list the two unit-test files that guard the frame-child resize path.
